## Requirements: Session-scoped Sandbox capability integrates Images management

**Status: In Discussion — approved direction for an updated interactive prototype, not production implementation.**

### Product decision (2026-11-13)

Sandbox entry **continues to require the current Session**; do not introduce a global Sandbox lobby or a Server-wide workspace navigation model. Consolidate the existing Server Images management UI as a Sandbox-internal section. Resource ownership **does not move**: the Server owns the global EROFS Image Registry/build/blob/grants, Agents own verified caches and distribution-readiness observations, and Sandbox consumes prepared images for one selected Session/Pane.

The current Sandbox product is **Overview + Images + Workspaces + Policies** (Workspaces is an independent Agent-owned reusable resource manager under #3407, not a synonym for global Nession Workspace). In Web, follow the candidate Claude-style capability layout: **Sandbox capability header with right-aligned first-level navigation**; inside the selected management area, **local left sidebar for second-level navigation**. App must retain one host-owned AppPageHeader/Back with compact capability-local navigation and no duplicate app header/back stack. The navigation is within the Session Workspace capability, not global application chrome.

| Sandbox section | Purpose | Local navigation / ownership |
|---|---|---|
| Overview | Current Session/Agent/Pane Sandbox state, active execution/readback, previews, quick entry to management | No second-level Sidebar required |
| Images | Server-global image library, build jobs, Agent cache/distribution observations | Library, Builds, Distribution; reuse the existing Server Images API/data/management view |
| Workspaces | Agent-local named, reusable managed workspace inventory and Project Location references (#3407) | List, details/create/reuse/inspect; current Session's Agent only |
| Policies | Per-Agent capability-gated Sandbox policy editing and inspection | Filesystem, Network, Linux Namespace, Cgroup v2, Seccomp; no Process/Resource/Syscall grouping; keep canonical `filesystem` key |

**Filesystem consumption is NOT global Image management:** `Policies → Filesystem` selects Base Runtime EROFS RootFS (implicit `/`), readonly tool EROFS mounts (explicit source→target), a selected Workspace (implicit `/workspace`), and preserves existing `filesystem.access.read/write` identity mapping. The detailed safe schema/mount rules are owned by #3405; the named Workspace lifecycle and reuse are owned by #3407. This Issue does not duplicate their source-of-truth.

### Verified baseline and migration

- Current `web/src/app/workspace/capabilities.ts` and `viewBindings.ts` treat `images` independently of Session while `sandbox` is only visible with a Session. Consolidate presentation so Sandbox remains Session-required, **but Server images still exist/are managed independently of Session** and a different Session on the same Server sees the same registry.
- `web/src/capabilities/images/components/ImagesWorkspace.tsx` currently owns Server Images management. Prefer reuse/composition, not backend duplication; conditional loading must not break when Session Agent is offline, except where Agent cache/distribution observation requires it.
- `web/src/capabilities/sandbox/components/SandboxWorkspace.tsx`, `SandboxComposer.tsx`, `SandboxPolicyTabs.tsx` own present six-peer-tabs model; the approved candidate replaces it with capability header → inner subnav.
- The accepted #3181 independently discoverable Images Workspace entry and its prototype now represent **superseded navigation**; keep #3181 delivery history and global API contract, but remove the separate entry as part of this new design when implemented.
- #3143's six peer tabs are a historical IA decision now revised. Preserve easy one-tap policy switching, unsaved draft persistence, precise back/history semantics and Inside read-only state; never create a multilevel dead-end.
- Capability and Agent support semantics remain as delivered by #3161 (available/unavailable/unknown; generation-bound; fail closed).

### Image Library detail interaction (confirmed 2026-11-13)

`Sandbox → Images → Image Library` is a **single list**, not a master-detail layout. Collapsed rows show name, image type, abbreviated digest and Server status. Clicking/tapping a row expands its details **immediately underneath the same row** (full Digest, image type, per-Agent cache status, default mount/RootFS target and applicable Filesystem action). One row expanded at a time; clicking the same row again collapses; moving to another row closes the previous detail. **Do not append a detached details card below the entire list.** Web uses keyboard-activatable disclosure buttons with `aria-expanded`; App uses the same tap flow and a compact single-column expanded layout. This is a prototype interaction change, with no Registry/Build/cache API change.

### Builds and Distribution progress (candidate UX; 2026-11-13)

**Builds / Server:** The durable asynchronous Build lifecycle and progress protocol implemented/accepted by [#3334](https://github.com/BestNathan/nession/issues/3334) are currently visible on `staging`, **not yet on `main`**. Use `server.image.build.submit/get/list/cancel/retry`, `server.image.build.updated`, and the persisted record on reconnect. The stage is `fetching/snapshotting/validating/packaging/publishing`, with truthful file/byte count, elapsed time, attempt/diagnostic and terminal status. `mkfs.erofs` exposes no meaningful total progress: display an indeterminate activity indicator during packaging, **never fabricate 90%**. Last bounded diagnostic is available; a full live operator-log stream is not guaranteed.

**Distribution / Agent:** The existing `ImageCacheStatus {digest,state,detail}` only observes `absent/preparing/verified/failed/unavailable`, and its `preparing` may mean a stale resumable `.part`, not an active transfer. It carries **no per-digest downloaded/total byte counters**. Cache machinery already supports ranged download, durable partial files and SHA-256 verified publication; a global completed-fetch counter is not the same as live progress. Add a minimally scoped Agent observation/progress contract keyed by `(agent_id,digest)`: `phase={absent,resumable,downloading,verifying,verified,failed}`, `downloaded_bytes` (partial file + streamed bytes), `total_bytes` (authorized Server Ready `ImageDescriptor.size_bytes` and validated response range), `active`, `updated_at`, bounded error. The Agent remains the authority and should push throttled progress and allow authoritative state reread after reconnect/restart. No generic Job DB or multi-Agent distribution scheduler. On completion of byte transfer, **Verifying is not mount-ready**; only SHA-256 verified atomic publish is Verified. A requested manual Prepare/Resume flow requires scoped grant authorization and an Agent API; a prototype button is not an existing production capability.

**Current prototype:** Builds stage/elapsed/counts, cancel/retry; Distribution per-Agent transferred byte ratio and optional percent **only when total is known**, resumable vs downloading vs verifying vs verified, with simulated transitions controlled **outside** the product viewport. These synthetic values are examples, not connected production telemetry. Do not infer globally distributed/fleet-ready from one Agent.

### Scope boundaries

- No change to Server-owned images, authenticated grants, immutable digests, Agent cache, EROFS assembly or Project ownership.
- No shared Images Picker model forced upon Project. Its independent declared image reference is unchanged.
- No global Sandbox workspace, no Session-less Sandbox entry, no coupling of image availability to one Agent's cache, and no claim that this prototype executes real builds/mounts.
- No arbitrary `mounts` target or filesystem access/composition coexistence until #3405 approves and OS-native verification proves it.

### Success Criteria

- [x] SC-01 With an active Session, Web/App Sandbox exposes Overview, Images, Workspaces and Policies as distinct capability-local sections. Without a Session, the Sandbox entry is unavailable; no separate Images Workspace entry remains in the candidate navigation.
- [x] SC-02 A user can navigate Images Library → Builds → Distribution, identify Server-global image status separately from current Agent's cache status, then return to Filesystem configuration without losing current Session or Policy draft. Image Library detail must expand inline under the selected list row (one at a time), never as a standalone panel after the list. Builds must show sourced stage, measured counters and elapsed (no invented total percentage); Distribution must separately show the selected Agent's cache bytes and digest verification, and never label a partial download as active or mount-ready.
- [x] SC-03 Web right-aligned header navigation and per-feature left sidebar; App one host-owned header with navigable compact sections, readable long lists, no duplicate Back, and no browser/App history stack on each section click; Inside policy views are read-only with trustworthy labels.
- [x] SC-04 The existing Images Server APIs/data/Project references and Agent cache/distribution ownership remain authoritative, and Session switch on one Server does not create a separate image registry.
- [x] SC-05 The existing Sandbox capability prototype `sandbox-capability-3124/` is revised **in place**, with interactive Web/App flows for all four sections and the three linked Requirements (#3405, #3407, this Issue), a source-pinned README, gallery entry and independent mock/published verification. The old `images-3181` mock is explicitly marked historical/superseded for navigation and links to the consolidated design.

**SC → scenario mapping:** SC-01/02/03 → SCN-02 (Chromium/Playwright UI interaction Case, current Session/Agent mock plus production implementation). SC-04 → SCN-01 (source/protocol ownership, relevant API/contract tests). SC-05 → SCN-08 (exact source SHA, prototype artifact, link and publication readback). Implemented UI acceptance is distinct from prototype fidelity.

## Prototype

- **Decision:** Required — major Web/App navigation/ownership revision across Server Images, Agent Workspaces and per-Agent Policies.
- **Owning directory:** Existing `sandbox-capability-3124/` on shared orphan `prototype` branch, **updated in place** (not a new duplicated mock); same direct design artifact for #3405 and #3407.
- **Immutable source:** https://github.com/BestNathan/nession/blob/27eb2ae0833168b39e4b648b42555c1972832d25/sandbox-capability-3124/index.html (commit `27eb2ae0833168b39e4b648b42555c1972832d25`); [source README](https://github.com/BestNathan/nession/blob/27eb2ae0833168b39e4b648b42555c1972832d25/sandbox-capability-3124/README.md).
- **Direct interactive preview:** https://bestnathan.github.io/nession/prototypes/sandbox-capability-3124/index.html — latest source SHA `27eb2ae0833168b39e4b648b42555c1972832d25` publication verification Pending; prior proof is for the previous revision.
- **Covered simulated flow:** Current Session Sandbox → Overview → Images Library / Builds / Distribution (same Server Registry, Agent cache status separated) → Workspaces inventory/create/reuse → Policies/FIlesystem RootFS, explicit tool mounts, named Workspace, access identity maps → native policy support → mock preflight/Enter/Inside/Return Native. Desktop header right-aligned first-level nav + local left subnav; App keeps one host header/Back and compact local navigation. No-Session removes Sandbox entry.
- **Prior mocks:** `images-3181/index.html` and its README are explicitly marked **historical for independent Images navigation**; Server data/API semantics remain authoritative. Old #3143 six-peer-policy-tab navigation is superseded in the shared Sandbox prototype.
- **Checks:** Previous mock state-check receipts are historical. Current #3405 five-section Filesystem IA passed 28/29 synthetic checks initially (the macOS status edge was fixed) and 12/12 final additional edge checks. New real Chromium visual proof remains Pending.
- **Published Pages proof (previous revision):** [Deploy / Public Pages #43395257696](https://github.com/BestNathan/nession/actions/runs/43395257696) **success**; authenticated workflow independently checked anonymous HTTPS `prototypes/manifest.json` source SHA `9fa4ace534d56765b8ad4d811fac8bd948a6131e` and Sandbox published HTML SHA-256 `c51971027b203b9321522789646a1195ede8df4f345f4fdb759102057553e4b8`. This verifies publication only; live Chromium UI review and production acceptance remain separate.
- **Published Pages proof (current revision 27eb2ae):** [Deploy / Public Pages #43426354374](https://github.com/BestNathan/nession/actions/runs/43426354374) **success**; anonymous HTTPS `prototypes/manifest.json` source SHA `27eb2ae0833168b39e4b648b42555c1972832d25`; published `sandbox-capability-3124/index.html` SHA-256 `520de263998cdbdb85b0770e32ad280650ca0ae4583afe668a4bbdbbfe254bf9` (the source differs only by the Pages CSP and source-link rewrite). `images-3181/README.md` at the same SHA opens with "HISTORICAL / NAVIGATION SUPERSEDED (2026-11-13)" and links to the revised `sandbox-capability-3124` mock.
- **2026-11-13 presentation revision:** Explanatory paragraphs no longer occupy the product viewport. RootFS, Mounts, Workspace, Access, Home, Agent support and field terms expose contextual help via hover (Web), keyboard focus, or click/tap (App), with `aria-expanded`/Escape behavior. Longer architecture notes now live in the external review-page details and mock README. Safety errors and deletion/Enter confirmation remain visible. The shared prototype directory remains unchanged.

- **Updated shared Filesystem IA (2026-11-13):** #3405 now orders RootFS / Mounts / Workspace / Access / Preview, removes standalone Home policy and excessive help, restricts Base Runtime selection to current Agent cache, provides image-default editable non-Base mounts, and always displays mapping Preview. These are prototype decisions, not production implementation.

- **Image Library revision:** List-only collapsed state; tap/click row for in-row details, tap again to collapse, opening another closes previous. Full digest, type, current Agent cache, mount target and applicable Filesystem action stay within the expanded row. Standalone detail below the list removed. Static synthetic UI checks **11/11 passed**, including Web/App and both RootFS/Mount actions; real Chromium visual proof pending.

- **Builds and Distribution revision:** Builds list now shows phase/elapsed/measured snapshot counts and Cancel/Retry. Distribution is per current Agent with resumable partial, byte progress and independent Verifying → Verified states. Synthetic stages advance through external reviewer-only controls. **18/18 simulated DOM/static checks passed**, including a cache-resume example and download-complete-before-verified safety condition; no real browser/protocol execution claimed. `staging` has #3334 Build lifecycle, `main` does not; Agent per-digest byte observations/Prepare API are a pending implementation seam.

## Product alignment

- [ ] Sandbox is discovered only inside a selected Session; preserves Terminal-first and capability-local contextual depth.
- [ ] Images remains one global Server registry/authoritative API while rendered in Sandbox.
- [ ] Workspaces and Filesystem Policy source/lifetime boundaries stay owned by #3407/#3405, not duplicate state inside Images.
- [ ] Web/App nav follows existing shell/back ownership without global UI redesign.
